papers.title: Phylogenomics, spatiotemporal transcriptional dynamics and Cis-regulatory architecture underlying the Portulaca oleracea antioxidant network under extreme salinity.
papers.abstract: Global soil salinization severely threatens agricultural productivity. Portulaca oleracea L., an extreme xerohalophyte, displays exceptional salinity tolerance, yet the transcriptional architecture coordinating its antioxidant defenses across organs and developmental stages remains unresolved. In this study, multi-tissue high-throughput RNA-Seq, quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) validation, comparative phylogenomics across 154 plant genomes, and condition-specific gene regulatory network (GRN) modeling were integrated to characterize 436 antioxidant loci in P. oleracea. Under chronic hypers
papers.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology
papers.summary: This study characterizes the antioxidant gene network of the extreme halophyte Portulaca oleracea under chronic high salinity using multi-tissue RNA-Seq, qRT-PCR validation, comparative phylogenomics across 154 plant genomes, and condition-specific gene regulatory network modeling. It identifies 436 antioxidant loci and reveals spatiotemporal transcriptional dynamics and cis-regulatory architecture underlying salinity tolerance across organs and developmental stages.

papers.title: Amino Acid Metabolic Signature Links Pediatric Environmental Enteric Dysfunction to Maternal-Fetal Growth Restriction Across Two Independent Cohorts.
papers.abstract: Environmental Enteric Dysfunction (EED) is a leading contributor to childhood stunting. Most EED literature derives from postnatal pediatric cohorts, leaving unclear how much of the metabolic signature reflects acquired intestinal pathology versus growth restriction originating earlier. We applied genome-scale metabolic modeling to explore whether metabolic features of pediatric EED overlap with those of maternal plasma proteomes associated with adverse early-life growth. Duodenal transcriptomics from the Study of Environmental Enteropathy and Malnutrition (SEEM; 52 children with EED, 24 contr
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study used genome-scale metabolic modeling to compare duodenal transcriptomic profiles from children with environmental enteric dysfunction (EED) against maternal plasma proteomic signatures linked to fetal growth restriction. The authors identified a shared amino acid metabolic signature across two independent cohorts, suggesting that some metabolic features of pediatric EED may reflect growth restriction originating in utero rather than solely acquired intestinal pathology.

papers.title: Nutrient control enables metabolic reconstruction of Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG and analysis of secretions.
papers.abstract: Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG (LGG) is an important gut commensal bacterial strain that has been extensively studied in both industrial and health settings. Despite its long history of study, a high-quality genome-scale metabolic network model (GEM) for LGG has yet to be reconstructed. Only automatically generated draft models have been published, which have notoriously limited functional accuracy. Furthermore, comprehensive nutrient requirements have not been established for well-controlled in vitro studies. Here, we present the first curated GEM for LGG using a new approach for reconstruct
papers.summary: The authors present the first manually curated genome-scale metabolic model for the probiotic gut bacterium Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG, built using a new reconstruction approach that incorporates experimentally determined nutrient requirements. They also establish defined nutrient conditions for controlled in vitro growth studies and use the model to analyze secretion products. This provides a more accurate computational framework for studying LGG metabolism than previously available draft models.

papers.title: Temporal multi-omics reveals regulatory transitions and renoprotective candidates in cisplatin-induced kidney injury.
papers.abstract: Cisplatin is a classic first-line platinum drug extensively used in chemotherapy for solid tumors, yet its clinical applications are limited by dose-dependent nephrotoxicity. The dynamic molecular mechanisms underlying cisplatin-induced kidney injury and regeneration remain incompletely understood. Here, we established two complementary mouse models, a single high-dose cisplatin (SHDC) model and a repeated low-dose cisplatin (RLDC) model, to recapitulate acute and progressive/persistent patterns of renal injury, respectively. Integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analyses reveal temporal tra
papers.summary: This study uses two mouse models of cisplatin-induced kidney injury (single high-dose and repeated low-dose) to profile transcriptomic and proteomic changes over time. The integrated multi-omics analysis uncovers temporal regulatory transitions and identifies candidate genes with renoprotective potential. The work provides a dynamic molecular map of injury and regeneration that could inform strategies to reduce cisplatin nephrotoxicity.

papers.title: Let there be multifunctionality: Uncovering the dynamical zoo of the AC-DC genetic circuit.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) govern many cell processes. While multistability and oscillations are common GRN dynamics, they are typically studied and engineered in isolation. Here, we challenge this separation using the AC-DC circuit, a minimal three-gene network that merges the classical toggle switch and repressilator. Using a thermodynamic formalism and Bayesian inference, we show that a single-inducer version of the circuit displays diverse multifunctional dynamics, including coexistence of oscillations and multistability. We explore robustness, classify emergent behaviors, and analyze
papers.summary: This study analyzes a minimal three-gene regulatory circuit (AC-DC) that combines a toggle switch and a repressilator, showing that a single-inducer version can exhibit multiple dynamical behaviors simultaneously, including coexisting oscillations and multistability. Using thermodynamic modeling and Bayesian inference, the authors map out a 'dynamical zoo' of behaviors and assess their robustness, challenging the usual practice of studying these dynamics in isolation.

papers.title: Robust identification of cell-cell communication heterogeneity in single cells.
papers.abstract: Cell-cell communication modulates cell fate decisions by relaying information across tissues and inducing intracellular responses mediated by gene regulatory networks. Although the inference of cell-cell communication from high-throughput data is gaining popularity, studying how communication pathways operate across biological scales and influence cell fate decisions remains challenging. Here, we present scRICH (robust identification of cell-cell communication heterogeneity in single cells), a computational framework that leverages single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data to unravel the he
papers.summary: The authors present scRICH, a computational framework for inferring cell-cell communication from single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data. It aims to robustly identify heterogeneity in communication pathways across cells and link these signals to downstream gene regulatory responses and cell fate decisions.

papers.title: Revisiting Ehrlich carcinoma in the era of precision oncology: bridging classical models with modern systems biology.
papers.abstract: Ehrlich carcinoma (EC) and its ascitic form, Ehrlich ascites carcinoma (EAC), are among the oldest and most widely used experimental tumor models in cancer research. Although they have traditionally been used for anticancer drug screening, their potential to address broader aspects of aggressive tumor biology has received comparatively less attention. EC/EAC exhibits several characteristics associated with advanced malignancy, including rapid tumor growth, angiogenesis, immune dysregulation, metabolic changes, therapeutic resistance, and complex interactions between the tumor and host. These f
papers.summary: This review argues that Ehrlich carcinoma and its ascitic form, long used mainly for anticancer drug screening, are underappreciated models for studying aggressive tumor biology. The authors highlight features such as rapid growth, angiogenesis, immune dysregulation, metabolic reprogramming, and therapeutic resistance, and propose integrating these classical models with modern systems biology approaches in precision oncology.

papers.title: Uncovering combination therapies for immune-mediated inflammatory diseases through systems biology analysis on longitudinal patient data.
papers.abstract: While targeted therapies have reshaped the clinical management of immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs), primary non-response remains a major obstacle for many patients. Combining two targeted therapies is an emerging strategy to overcome this therapeutic ceiling, but the number of possible drug pairs makes prioritization difficult. For this objective, we present mitigation of non-response signature (MNRS), a computational approach that uses longitudinal blood transcriptomic data from six IMIDs treated with different targeted therapies to identify the most promising drug combinations.
papers.summary: The authors present MNRS, a computational method that uses longitudinal blood transcriptomic data from patients with six immune-mediated inflammatory diseases to prioritize combination therapies that could overcome primary non-response to targeted drugs. By identifying drug pairs that counteract non-response signatures, the approach offers a systems-biology framework for narrowing the large space of possible combinations.

papers.title: Modeling microbiome modulation of tumor metabolic networks to predict synergistic therapies.
papers.abstract: Differences in microbiome composition profoundly influence drug response, yet methods to model the metabolic impact of microbes on host cells and therapeutics remain limited. We present a microbiome-aware computational framework combining machine learning and genome-scale metabolic models to predict combination therapies for colorectal cancer (CRC) in the presence of Fusobacterium nucleatum (Fn) and other pathogenic, probiotic, and commensal microbes. The model learned predictive metabolic flux signatures from 6,514 drug combination profiles in CRC cell lines and predicted synergistic drug com
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational framework that combines machine learning with genome-scale metabolic models to predict how microbiome composition affects tumor metabolism and drug response in colorectal cancer. The model was trained on 6,514 drug combination profiles and can predict synergistic drug combinations in the presence of Fusobacterium nucleatum and other microbes.

papers.title: A single-nucleus transcriptomic atlas reveals the endodermal gene regulatory network underlying Arabidopsis stem gravitropism.
papers.abstract: Gravitropism redirects plant organ growth by converting gravity perception into asymmetric growth initiated in endodermal statocytes. Although the C2H2-type zinc finger transcription factor SHOOT GRAVITROPISM 5 (SGR5), also known as INDETERMINATE DOMAIN 15 (IDD15), is essential for shoot gravitropism, the transcriptional mechanisms linking gravity perception to directional growth remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study generated a single-nucleus transcriptomic atlas of the Arabidopsis stem to map the gene regulatory network controlling gravitropism. The authors identify endodermal cell populations and characterize how the transcription factor SGR5/IDD15 orchestrates the transcriptional program linking gravity perception in statocytes to asymmetric growth. The atlas provides a cell-type-resolved framework for understanding how plants convert a physical gravity signal into directional organ bending.

papers.title: PIANO enables generative modeling of gene expression and scales multi-omics integration to 100 million cells.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA technologies enable the routine acquisition of transcriptomic atlases. However, these molecular profiles are influenced by overlapping sources of variation. Since these covariates confound comparisons, data integration is the first step in most analyses. Three challenges remain: correcting strong batch effects, scaling to millions of cells, and modeling how covariates influence gene expression. To address these challenges, we developed PIANO, probabilistic inference autoencoder networks for multi-omics, a deep learning framework whose central feature is a generative model of ge
papers.summary: PIANO is a deep learning framework that uses a generative model of gene expression to integrate single-cell multi-omics data. It addresses three key challenges in the field: correcting strong batch effects, scaling analyses to millions of cells (demonstrated up to 100 million), and explicitly modeling how covariates influence gene expression. This enables more accurate comparisons across large transcriptomic atlases.

papers.title: Host-like temperature unlocks glucose uptake and metabolism in pathogenic Leptospira.
papers.abstract: Pathogenic Leptospira transitions between environmental reservoirs and mammalian hosts, exposing the bacterium to distinct temperature conditions. Although Leptospira is generally considered to rely primarily on long-chain fatty acids for growth and to have limited capacity to use glucose, whether host-like temperature alters glucose-associated metabolic capacity remains unclear. Here, we used transcriptome-integrated genome-scale metabolic modeling to examine temperature-dependent metabolic states in pathogenic Leptospira. Models contextualized with transcriptomic data from cultures at 37°C p
papers.summary: Using transcriptome-integrated genome-scale metabolic modeling, the authors show that pathogenic Leptospira grown at host-like temperature (37°C) upregulates glucose uptake and metabolism, contrary to the long-held view that these bacteria rely mainly on fatty acids and have limited glucose use. This temperature-dependent metabolic shift may be important for survival and virulence within mammalian hosts.

papers.title: Stochasticity in Metabolism: Oxidative Stress Response Phenotypes As Emergent Consequences of Network Topology.
papers.abstract: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) are ubiquitous yet elusive due to their reactivity and short half-lives, making simulation essential for mechanistic insight. Traditional ROS modeling has been confined to small ODE frameworks limited by kinetic-parameter scarcity. Here, we recast ROS dynamics as a flux-balance analysis (FBA) optimization problem using COBRA and CPLEX, augmenting the Escherichia coli iJO1366 genome-scale model with 84 spontaneous oxidation, 14 redox, and 9 detoxification reactions, targeting three ROS species: hydroxyl radicals, superoxide, and hydrogen peroxide (H2O2). We also fo
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors extend the E. coli genome-scale metabolic model iJO1366 with reactions for ROS production, redox balance, and detoxification, then use flux-balance analysis to simulate ROS dynamics. They show that oxidative stress response phenotypes can emerge from network topology and stochasticity rather than from detailed kinetic parameters.

papers.title: scPhyloGRN: gene regulatory network inference guided by lineage topology in single-cell developmental data.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network (GRN) inference from single-cell transcriptomes is complicated by expression patterns associated with both cell state and shared ancestry. Cellular phylogenies provide developmental context, but incorporating relationships among individual cells into gene-level regulatory inference remains challenging.
papers.summary: scPhyloGRN is a new method that infers gene regulatory networks from single-cell developmental transcriptomes by using the lineage topology (cellular phylogeny) as a guide, separating expression variation due to shared ancestry from that due to cell state. This allows more accurate identification of gene-level regulatory relationships in differentiating cells.

papers.title: Engineering rhizosphere microbial consortia for soil bioremediation: Mechanisms, field constraints, and evidence-based design.
papers.abstract: Soil contamination continues to threaten ecosystem health and agricultural productivity worldwide. However, rhizosphere-mediated bioremediation has emerged as a nature-inspired, sustainable approach for mitigating these impacts. This review advocates field-scale implementation of rhizosphere microbiome engineering by exploiting interactions among plants, microorganisms, and soil. Unlike previous reviews that primarily summarize rhizosphere-mediated remediation processes, it integrates mechanistic, ecological, and engineering perspectives to identify critical barriers limiting field performance
papers.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology
papers.summary: This review argues for moving rhizosphere microbiome engineering from laboratory studies to field-scale soil bioremediation. It integrates mechanistic, ecological, and engineering perspectives to identify the key barriers that limit real-world performance, and proposes evidence-based design principles for constructing plant-microbe consortia. The emphasis is on exploiting plant-microbe-soil interactions rather than simply cataloguing remediation processes.

papers.title: A time-resolved single-nucleus atlas of cochlear aging reveals biphasic inflammaging and Tbx2-dependent inner hair cell maintenance.
papers.abstract: Age-related hearing loss (ARHL) is the most prevalent sensory deficit in older adults, yet its molecular progression remains poorly resolved. Few cochlear single-cell studies have integrated cell-cell communication, gene regulatory network (GRN) reconstruction, and cross-cohort bulk validation into one temporal framework.
papers.summary: This study builds a time-resolved single-nucleus atlas of the aging mouse cochlea, tracking how different cell types change across the lifespan. It identifies two distinct phases of age-related inflammation (inflammaging) and shows that the transcription factor Tbx2 is required for maintaining inner hair cells. The work integrates cell-cell communication analysis, gene regulatory network reconstruction, and bulk RNA-seq validation across cohorts.

papers.title: Genome-scale metabolic model analysis of Korean Campylobacter jejuni isolates reveals lineage-level metabolic structure.
papers.abstract: Genome-scale metabolic models (GSMMs) of Campylobacter jejuni (C. jejuni) have been studied mainly for reference strains, and their characteristics at the lineage level remain poorly understood. We reconstructed GSMMs for 86 C. jejuni isolates collected in Korea using gapseq and analyzed them together with in vitro substrate utilization data for seven substrates measured on the same isolates. Strain-specific GSMMs clustered by clonal complex (CC): in all nine CCs with ≥ 2 isolates the mean within-CC Jaccard distance was smaller than the mean between-CC distance; across all strain pairs the med
papers.summary: The authors reconstructed genome-scale metabolic models for 86 Korean Campylobacter jejuni isolates and found that the models cluster by clonal complex, indicating lineage-level metabolic structure. They validated these models against in vitro substrate utilization data for seven substrates measured on the same isolates. This shows that metabolic model structure reflects phylogenetic lineage in this pathogen.

papers.title: Protamine gene expression is associated with sperm motility in rams: An integrative experimental and gene network analysis.
papers.abstract: Protamine 1 (PRM1) and protamine 2 (PRM2) are essential regulators of sperm chromatin condensation and genome integrity, and their dysregulation has been associated with impaired male fertility. However, their role in rams remains insufficiently characterized. This study investigated the relationship between protamine gene expression and semen quality in rams and explored their potential upstream regulatory mechanisms using gene regulatory network (GRN) analysis. Fifteen ejaculates from five rams were analyzed. Based on total sperm motility using computer-assisted sperm analysis (CASA), ejacul
papers.summary: This study examined whether expression levels of the protamine genes PRM1 and PRM2 relate to semen quality in rams, using 15 ejaculates from five animals and computer-assisted sperm analysis. The authors report that protamine gene expression is associated with sperm motility and use gene regulatory network analysis to propose upstream regulators. The work extends protamine biology from well-studied species into ram reproduction, though the sample size is small.

papers.title: Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network inference methods routinely disagree about individual edges, and practitioners resolve those conflicts by choosing one method or averaging them all. We ask whether the conflict can instead be arbitrated per edge. A gradient-boosted classifier is trained on the raw scores that ten inference methods-correlation-based, information-theoretic, sparse-regression and tree-ensemble, including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR and ARACNe-assign to each candidate regulator-target pair, so that the weight given to each method varies from edge to edge. Across six single-cell perturbation scre
papers.summary: The authors propose a per-edge arbitration approach for gene regulatory network inference, training a gradient-boosted classifier on the raw scores from ten different inference methods so that each method's weight varies by regulator-target pair rather than being fixed globally. They also develop a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflicts. Evaluated across six single-cell perturbation screens, this score-level meta-classifier offers an alternative to choosing one method or averaging all methods.

papers.title: Comparative phylogenomics and transcriptional regulatory networks of AQPs, HSPs, and LEA proteins in salt-stressed Portulaca oleracea.
papers.abstract: Soil salinization severely threatens global food security, necessitating systematic investigations of halophytes like Portulaca oleracea to decode the molecular mechanisms of environmental resilience. Utilizing an integrated framework of deep learning-based genome annotation (58,817 predicted genes; 96.5% BUSCO completeness), multi-tissue RNA-Seq, phylogenomics, and gene regulatory network (GRN) inference, the synergistic orchestration of 78 aquaporins (AQPs), 525 heat shock proteins (HSPs), and 119 late embryogenesis abundant (LEA) proteins was elucidated. The active transcriptome, encompassi
papers.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology
papers.summary: This study combines deep learning-based genome annotation, multi-tissue RNA-Seq, phylogenomics, and gene regulatory network inference to characterize aquaporins, heat shock proteins, and LEA proteins in the halophyte Portulaca oleracea under salt stress. It reports a high-quality annotated genome (58,817 genes, 96.5% BUSCO completeness) and reveals coordinated transcriptional regulation of these stress-responsive gene families. The work provides a resource for understanding salt tolerance mechanisms in halophytes.

papers.title: Decoding the epithelial-stromal interactome in allergic rhinitis through single-cell multiomics integration.
papers.abstract: Allergic rhinitis (AR) is a prevalent chronic condition, yet the cellular and molecular changes associated with its pathogenesis remain incompletely understood.
papers.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell multiomics data to map the epithelial-stromal interactome in allergic rhinitis, revealing cellular and molecular changes underlying disease pathogenesis. The findings provide a comprehensive atlas of cell-cell communication in AR, highlighting key signaling pathways between epithelial and stromal compartments.

papers.title: Endothelial SLC25A13 links glutamine metabolism to angiogenesis.
papers.abstract: Attention to exploring endothelial cell (EC) metabolism is increasing, but a holistic perspective on the metabolic adaptations of ECs during angiogenic proliferation is still missing. Here, we use a previously in-house developed computational EC-adapted genome-scale metabolic model that recapitulates known metabolic features in proliferating ECs to predict novel pathways central to biomass synthesis. We unveil the metabolic function of the glutamate-aspartate antiporter SLC25A13, previously overlooked in ECs, as a key regulator of glutamine utilization and provide evidence regarding its contri
papers.summary: Using a computational genome-scale metabolic model tailored to endothelial cells, the authors predicted and then experimentally validated that the mitochondrial glutamate-aspartate antiporter SLC25A13 is a key regulator of glutamine utilization during angiogenesis. This previously overlooked transporter supports biomass synthesis in proliferating endothelial cells, linking glutamine metabolism to new blood vessel formation.

papers.title: A metabolic model based on a pangenome core reveals putative conserved biochemical features of the phytopathogen Xylella fastidiosa.
papers.abstract: Xylella fastidiosa is a xylem-limited phytopathogenic bacterium responsible for severe diseases in many economically important crops. Despite its impact, its metabolism remains poorly characterized due to fastidious growth and the limited availability of defined culture media. Here, we reconstruct the first pangenome-based genome-scale metabolic model for X. fastidiosa, integrating conserved metabolic functions from 18 strains across five subspecies. The resulting consensus model, iXfcore, is manually curated and used to explore the species' metabolic capabilities. Model simulations predict mi
papers.summary: Researchers built the first genome-scale metabolic model for the plant pathogen Xylella fastidiosa based on conserved genes across 18 strains and five subspecies. The manually curated model, iXfcore, predicts metabolic capabilities and highlights conserved biochemical features that may guide future culture media design and study of this hard-to-grow bacterium.

papers.title: Hybrid genome‑scale metabolic modeling and machine learning reveal cost‑efficient strategies for phototrophic polyhydroxybutyrate production in Rhodopseudomonas palustris.
papers.abstract: Plastic pollution from fossil-based materials is a major global environmental challenge. Microbially derived bioplastics, such as polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB), offer a promising biodegradable alternative. However, the high substrate and operational costs of PHB production remain a major barrier to large-scale deployment. Optimizing PHB synthesis requires navigating a multidimensional design space of metabolic, nutritional, and operational variables, which is impractical to explore experimentally. This study presents an integrated computational framework that combines a genome-scale metabolic mode
papers.summary: This study combines a genome-scale metabolic model of Rhodopseudomonas palustris with machine learning to explore the design space for phototrophic polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB) production. The hybrid framework identifies cost-efficient strategies for boosting PHB synthesis across metabolic, nutritional, and operational variables that would be impractical to test experimentally. It offers a computational route to lowering substrate and operational costs for biodegradable bioplastic production.

papers.title: Multi-omic analysis reveals maturation programs in human pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes during long-term culture.
papers.abstract: Human pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hPSC-CMs) hold tremendous promise for disease modeling, drug discovery, and cardiac regenerative therapies. However, the immature phenotype of hPSC-CMs remains a major barrier limiting their translational utility. Here, we performed integrated multi-omic profiling to identify molecular pathways and regulatory programs associated with hPSC-CM maturation during long-term culture. hPSC-CMs were cultured for 113 days and analyzed using metabolomics, proteomics, and transcriptomics across progressive stages of maturation. Long-term culture induced
papers.journal: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology
papers.summary: This study used integrated metabolomics, proteomics, and transcriptomics to profile human pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hPSC-CMs) over 113 days of culture, identifying molecular pathways and regulatory programs that drive maturation. Long-term culture induced progressive maturation-associated changes across multiple omic layers, offering a roadmap for understanding and potentially overcoming the immature phenotype that limits translational use of hPSC-CMs.

papers.title: TREM2 signaling in cardiovascular disease: macrophage heterogeneity, timing, and therapeutic opportunity.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, with pathogenesis extending beyond hemodynamic derangements to involve chronic, maladaptive immune-metabolic crosstalk. Macrophage functional identity has evolved beyond the M1/M2 paradigm toward a model of high heterogeneity and dynamic plasticity, wherein Triggering Receptor Expressed on Myeloid Cells 2 (TREM2) serves as a pivotal molecular hub.
papers.summary: This review argues that TREM2 acts as a central molecular hub governing macrophage heterogeneity and plasticity in cardiovascular disease, moving beyond the simple M1/M2 classification. It emphasizes the importance of timing of TREM2 signaling and highlights therapeutic opportunities for targeting it in cardiovascular conditions.

papers.title: Causality analysis of toxicological mechanisms in networked systems such as adverse outcome pathway networks.
papers.abstract: This paper examines why robust causality assessment is central to toxicology yet increasingly difficult in networked biological systems, including Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) networks and multi-omics datasets. Classical causal frameworks (e.g., Koch/Dale reasoning and Bradford Hill-type considerations) remain useful for scoping, but they offer limited operational guidance for multifactorial, nonlinear, and feedback-dominated mechanisms. We therefore synthesize a modern toolbox for causality analysis in toxicology spanning directed acyclic graphs for explicit causal assumptions, quantitative
papers.summary: This review argues that traditional causality frameworks like Koch's postulates and Bradford Hill criteria are insufficient for analyzing toxicological mechanisms in complex networked systems such as Adverse Outcome Pathway networks and multi-omics data. The authors synthesize a modern causality toolbox—including directed acyclic graphs, quantitative causal inference methods, and network-based approaches—to better handle multifactorial, nonlinear, and feedback-driven mechanisms. The paper provides operational guidance for toxicologists applying causal reasoning to networked biological data.

papers.title: Neutrophil-microglia communication through the C3-C3aR1 axis contributes to secondary neuroinflammation after traumatic brain injury.
papers.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) triggers a rapidly evolving neuroinflammatory response that contributes to secondary brain injury. Although infiltrating leukocytes and resident microglia are both prominent components of this response, the cellular signals that connect peripheral immune-cell recruitment to microglial state remodeling remain incompletely defined.
papers.summary: This study investigates how peripheral immune cells and brain-resident microglia communicate after traumatic brain injury to drive secondary neuroinflammation. The authors identify the complement C3-C3aR1 signaling axis as a key mediator of neutrophil-microglia crosstalk, linking infiltrating neutrophils to microglial state changes that worsen secondary brain injury.

papers.title: Identification of metabolic vulnerabilities and synthetic lethal targets utilizing artificial intelligence-driven precision medicine.
papers.abstract: Cancer metabolism is highly plastic, and most attempts to turn that plasticity into a therapeutic target fail for a specific, recurring reason: a computational prediction of a metabolic vulnerability is not the same evidentiary object as an experimentally confirmed one, and the two are routinely discussed as if they were interchangeable. This review takes that distinction as its starting point rather than its conclusion. Artificial intelligence and genome-scale systems biology have made it easy to generate metabolic hypotheses at a scale no experimental program could match - machine learning m
papers.summary: This review argues that AI-driven computational predictions of cancer metabolic vulnerabilities are fundamentally different from experimentally confirmed ones, yet the field routinely conflates the two. It examines how machine learning and genome-scale metabolic modeling generate hypotheses at scale, and calls for clearer evidentiary standards before synthetic lethal targets are treated as validated.

papers.title: ExposomeMap-PM: fine and ultrafine particle-induced toxicity - from adverse outcome pathways to systems biomedicine disease models.
papers.abstract: Air pollution is one of the leading global environmental health risks, associated with millions of premature deaths annually. It represents a substantial share of the global disease burden. Despite well-established epidemiological associations, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain only partially understood. There is a need for systematic approaches toward mechanistic understanding that connect particulate matter exposure to downstream pathways and pathophysiological effects.
papers.summary: This paper presents ExposomeMap-PM, a framework that maps fine and ultrafine particulate matter exposure to molecular mechanisms and downstream disease outcomes using adverse outcome pathway concepts and systems biomedicine modeling. It aims to systematically connect air pollution exposure to pathophysiological effects, addressing the gap between epidemiological associations and mechanistic understanding.

papers.title: Bringing translational structure to complex immune-mediated conditions: the ACT (Activation-Constraint-Tissue Context) framework for divergent phenotypes.
papers.abstract: Immune-mediated outcomes diverge across individuals with similar genetic backgrounds and environmental exposures, reflecting trajectories through a dynamic, context-dependent, and partially stochastic state space rather than fixed molecular endpoints. Despite advances in systems immunology, computational modeling, and multi-omic profiling, translating this complexity into clinically actionable reasoning remains difficult: these disciplines generate increasingly detailed representations of immune behavior that deepen mechanistic understanding while raising barriers to integration across clinica
papers.summary: The authors propose the ACT (Activation-Constraint-Tissue Context) framework as a conceptual model for understanding why individuals with similar genetic and environmental backgrounds develop divergent immune-mediated phenotypes. They argue that immune outcomes reflect trajectories through a dynamic, context-dependent, partially stochastic state space rather than fixed molecular endpoints, and that current systems immunology and multi-omic approaches generate detailed but poorly integrated representations that hinder clinical translation. The framework aims to provide a translational structure for integrating these complex data into clinically actionable reasoning.
